items.q: D-glucose and D-galactose differ stereochemically in the spatial configuration around which single carbon atom, defining them as epimers?
items.exp: D-glucose and D-galactose are C-4 epimers. D-glucose and D-mannose are C-2 epimers. Inversion at C-1 represents anomerism upon ring closure.
r: Correct. Glucose and galactose are C-4 epimers.
Incorrect. Inversion at C-2 creates D-mannose.
Incorrect. C-3 configuration is identical in both.
Incorrect. C-1 inversion represents alpha/beta anomers.
items.kp: D-glucose and D-galactose are C-4 epimers; D-glucose and D-mannose are C-2 epimers.

items.q: Why is sucrose considered a non-reducing sugar that yields a negative result on Benedict and Fehling copper reduction tests?
o: Both anomeric carbon atoms (C-1 of glucose and C-2 of fructose) are linked in the glycosidic bond
It lacks hydroxyl groups on its ring carbons
It contains only pentose sugars that cannot reduce copper
It forms insoluble crystals that prevent reagent contact
items.exp: Sucrose is formed by an alpha-1,beta-2 glycosidic bond between the anomeric C-1 of glucose and anomeric C-2 of fructose. With neither anomeric carbon free to open into an aldehyde/ketone, it cannot reduce Cu2+.
r: Correct. Both anomeric carbons are engaged in the glycosidic bond, leaving no free hemiacetal.
Incorrect. It possesses numerous free hydroxyl groups.
Incorrect. It consists of glucose (hexose) and fructose (hexose).
Incorrect. Sucrose is highly water-soluble.
items.kp: Sucrose is non-reducing because its alpha-1,beta-2 glycosidic bond engages the anomeric carbons of both glucose and fructose.

items.q: Which polyunsaturated fatty acid containing 18 carbons and two cis-double bonds is an essential dietary fatty acid because humans lack delta-12 and delta-15 desaturases?
items.exp: Linoleic acid (18:2, delta-9,12) is an essential omega-6 fatty acid. Humans cannot introduce double bonds beyond carbon 9, making dietary linoleic and alpha-linolenic acids mandatory.
r: Correct. Linoleic acid (18:2) is an essential omega-6 fatty acid.
Incorrect. Alpha-linolenic acid has 3 double bonds (18:3).
Incorrect. Oleic acid is monounsaturated (18:1) and non-essential.
Incorrect. Arachidonic acid has 20 carbons and can be made from linoleic acid.
items.kp: Linoleic acid (18:2, n-6) and alpha-linolenic acid (18:3, n-3) are essential dietary fatty acids because humans cannot desaturate beyond carbon 9.

items.q: What is the structural effect of a cis-double bond compared to a trans-double bond in a fatty acid hydrocarbon chain?
o: Introduces a 30-degree rigid kink that disrupts tight packing and increases membrane fluidity
Straightens the carbon chain, allowing denser paracrystalline packing
Increases the melting point above that of saturated fatty acids
Enables spontaneous cleavage into free radical fragments
items.exp: A cis-double bond creates a rigid 30-degree kink in the hydrocarbon chain, preventing tight parallel packing of lipids, which lowers the melting temperature and increases membrane fluidity.
r: Correct. Cis-double bonds introduce kinks that disrupt packing and boost fluidity.
Incorrect. Trans-double bonds and saturated chains adopt straight geometries.
Incorrect. Cis-double bonds lower the melting point.
Incorrect. Double bonds do not spontaneously fragment under normal conditions.
items.kp: Cis-double bonds introduce rigid kinks in fatty acid chains, preventing dense packing and increasing biological membrane fluidity.

items.q: Why are triacylglycerols a far more efficient long-term energy storage vehicle than glycogen in mammalian adipose tissue?
o: They are stored anhydrously and yield 37 kJ/g upon oxidation, compared to 17 kJ/g for hydrated glycogen
They require zero oxygen for complete catabolic oxidation
They can be converted directly to glucose in skeletal muscle
They are soluble in blood without carrier proteins
items.exp: Triacylglycerols are neutral and hydrophobic, stored without water of hydration (glycogen binds twice its weight in water) and are highly reduced, yielding 37 kJ/g (9 kcal/g) versus 17 kJ/g (4 kcal/g) for carbohydrates.
r: Correct. Triacylglycerols are anhydrous and yield over twice the caloric density per gram.
Incorrect. Fatty acid oxidation requires substantial oxygen.
Incorrect. Odd-chain only yields minimal propionate; muscle cannot make glucose from fats.
Incorrect. Lipids require albumin and lipoproteins for transport.
items.kp: Triacylglycerols provide over twice the energy density of carbohydrates (37 vs 17 kJ/g) and are stored completely anhydrously in adipocytes.

items.q: Intestinal brush border lactase hydrolyzes lactose into which two monosaccharide constituents?
items.exp: Lactose is a disaccharide of beta-D-galactopyranosyl-(1->4)-D-glucopyranose. Lactase (beta-galactosidase) hydrolyzes this beta-1,4 bond to release free D-galactose and D-glucose.
r: Correct. Lactose hydrolyzes into glucose and galactose.
Incorrect. Glucose and fructose form sucrose.
Incorrect. Two glucose molecules form maltose.
Incorrect. Galactose and fructose do not form lactose.
items.kp: Brush border lactase cleaves the beta-1,4 glycosidic bond of lactose into free D-glucose and D-galactose.

items.q: In glycogen, linear chains of glucose residues are joined by alpha-1,4 bonds, whereas branch points are formed by which linkage?
items.exp: Glycogen branches occur approximately every 8 to 12 residues and are formed by alpha-1,6-glycosidic linkages introduced by the branching enzyme (amylo-alpha-1,4->1,6-transglucosidase).
r: Correct. Glycogen branch points are alpha-1,6 linkages.
Incorrect. Beta-1,4 bonds occur in cellulose and lactose.
Incorrect. Alpha-1,2 bonds occur in sucrose.
Incorrect. Beta-1,6 linkages occur in certain fungal glucans.
items.kp: Glycogen branches are joined by alpha-1,6-glycosidic linkages, introduced every 8 to 12 glucose units along alpha-1,4 linear chains.

items.q: Hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL) in adipose tissue is phosphorylated and activated during fasting in response to which hormonal stimulation?
o: Epinephrine and Glucagon via cyclic AMP and Protein Kinase A
items.exp: During fasting or stress, glucagon and epinephrine bind Gs-coupled receptors, elevating cAMP and activating PKA. PKA phosphorylates HSL and perilipin, exposing lipid droplets to lipolysis.
r: Correct. Glucagon and epinephrine stimulate PKA phosphorylation of HSL.
Incorrect. Insulin activates PP1, which dephosphorylates and inhibits HSL.
Incorrect. Growth hormone has permissive long-term effects.
Incorrect. Cortisol induces lipase expression transcriptionally.
items.kp: Hormone-sensitive lipase is phosphorylated and activated by PKA in response to epinephrine and glucagon, promoting triacylglycerol lipolysis.

items.q: A newborn is evaluated for cataracts, hepatosplenomegaly, and failure to thrive after breast milk feeding. Urine is positive for reducing substances but negative on glucose oxidase dipstick. Which enzyme is deficient?
items.exp: Classic galactosemia results from GALT deficiency, leading to toxic accumulation of galactose-1-phosphate and galactitol. Unmetabolized galactose is a reducing sugar (Benedict positive) but glucose dipstick negative.
r: Correct. GALT deficiency causes classic galactosemia with cataracts, liver failure, and galactosuria.
Incorrect. Galactokinase deficiency causes isolated cataracts without hepatosplenomegaly.
Incorrect. Fructokinase deficiency is asymptomatic essential fructosuria.
Incorrect. Aldolase B deficiency is hereditary fructose intolerance triggered by fructose/sucrose, not milk lactose.
items.kp: Classic galactosemia (GALT deficiency) manifests after milk feeding with cataracts, liver dysfunction, and urine positive for reducing sugars but negative for glucose.

items.q: Which essential fatty acid serves as the direct biochemical precursor for the synthesis of arachidonic acid (20:4, n-6) in human hepatocytes?
items.exp: Linoleic acid undergoes delta-6 desaturation, elongation by two carbons, and delta-5 desaturation to generate arachidonic acid (20:4, n-6), the precursor for pro-inflammatory eicosanoids.
r: Correct. Linoleic acid is elongated and desaturated to produce arachidonic acid.
Incorrect. Alpha-linolenic acid yields EPA and DHA (omega-3).
Incorrect. Oleic acid yields Mead acid during essential fatty acid deficiency.
Incorrect. Palmitic acid is a saturated fatty acid.
